item.title: Talawanda Baseball Winter Clinic for Grades K-8
item.description:
The Talawanda Baseball Winter Clinic is a two-day clinic for boys and girls in grades K-8, held January 18-19, 9:00 AM-11:00 AM at THS Gymnasium. Varsity and junior-varsity staff will teach hitting, fielding, throwing, and pitching/catching. Bring a baseball glove, water bottle, bat, and helmet. Cost: $30 for one day or $50 for two days (take $10 off for each additional family member). Register by January 5th to receive a clinic T-shirt. Sign up at https://forms.gle/cgfxGjopmEKmrXpD8 or check in on January 19th. Contact: lykinsm@talawanda.org

item.title: Mental Health Resources and Support Information
item.description:
The Mental Health Corner provides information about rumination (repetitive negative thoughts that are hard to control and cause emotional distress) and strategies to combat it. Recommended coping strategies include moving to a different location, reading or playing games, focusing on spiritual practices, taking walks outside, speaking to someone you trust, listening to uplifting music, and practicing self-compassion. Signs that therapy might be needed for students include behavior changes, emotional struggles, anger management issues, social/school problems, physical symptoms, regressions, risky behavior, or abnormal thoughts. Parents should contact school counselors to connect with integrated services. Immediate crisis resources include: - Butler County Crisis Line: (513)881-7180 - Psychiatric Intake Response Center (PIRC): (513)636-4124

item.title: Talawanda Preschool Application Lottery 2026/2027
item.description:
Applications are now open for the Talawanda Preschool lottery for the 2026/2027 school year. Typically developing children will enter the program through a lottery to fill limited spaces. Applications must be completed by January 31, 2026, and the lottery will be held on February 13, 2026. Families will be notified of their placement or waitlist status after the lottery date. Questions can be sent to Preschool Coordinator Beth Fuechsl at fuechsle@talawanda.org.

item.title: Flu and Seasonal Illness Health Reminder
item.description:
The school is experiencing an increase in flu and seasonal illnesses. Keep your child home if they have: a fever (100°F or higher), vomiting/diarrhea, significant cough, sore throat with fever, body aches, extreme fatigue, or flu-like symptoms. Return to school only after: fever-free for 24 hours without medication AND symptom-free for 24 hours after vomiting or diarrhea.

item.title: Office Procedures for Absences and Medical Forms
item.description:
Two important office procedures for families: - Homework requests for absences: If your student will miss multiple days of school (illness, vacation, injury), request work from the office or teachers several days in advance—calling the day before is not sufficient time. - Medical forms (Vanderbilt Forms): Submit medical forms that need teacher completion to the guidance counselors, not directly to teachers. Counselors will distribute them to teachers and send completed forms directly to the doctor's office before appointments.

item.title: Food Resources and Community Meal Information
item.description:
The Talawanda School District provides several food assistance resources for families in need: - Little Free Pantries available 24/7 outside every TSD building, restocked weekly - Backpack Program offers small weekly food bags on Thursdays/Fridays at elementary buildings (contact building Social Worker) - Emergency Food Boxes available for pick-up or delivery within 24 hours - Access a calendar of community meals and TOPPS schedule, a list of all Butler County food pantries, and up-to-date SNAP information through the provided links
